title: A virtual call explained
description:
Show how a virtual call finds its function through the vtable.

```
class Shape { virtual ~Shape(); virtual double area(); virtual void draw(); }
call [rax+0x10] on a Shape* -> slot 2 -> draw
Circle's vtable: ~Circle, Circle::area, Shape::draw (not overridden)
```
hints: Slot = offset / 8; the object's first 8 bytes hold the pointer to its class's table (lesson 2.05).
MSVC puts the destructor where it is declared; check the order with your own compiled class in a debugger.
requirements: Model a vtable as an array of function names per class; a derived class copies its base's and replaces what it overrides.
Turn an offset like `[rax+0x10]` into a slot number (8 bytes per slot) and a name.
stretch: Add multiple inheritance, where an object has two vtable pointers.
